newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, focus on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, focus on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate early trading on Monday on the back of a slightly tight money market, dealers said.
They said early focus was on liquidity, with speculation of a band widening seen waning for now.
One European bank dealer said overnight rates' jump on Friday seemed to unsettle some small banks, which boosted their rupiah reserves and kept overnight money at 14.5 percent.
Overnight money soared to a high of 45 percent before settling at 40 percent late on Friday. Dealers said the jump was technical and not due to fundamental changes.

The European bank dealer said talk of a band widening, which was the focus last Thursday and Friday, seemed to weaken as local operators were not convinced of an immenent move by the central bank to widen the band from the current eight percent. He said offshore players were keeping some pressure on the dollar, but the currency edged up after Jakarta opened.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.00/30.25 at 0230 GMT against an opening of 2,429.80/30.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,428.40/28.80 and 2,429.00/29.25, respectively.
Short-term swaps were driven higher by an uptrend in short-term money. Overnight swaps were at 0.50/0.55 points.
One-month swaps were at 14.00/14.75, two at 26.5/28.0, three at 40.0/41.5 and six at 81.0/83.0 points.
One Japanese bank dealer said operators were also waiting for the announcement of an economic deregulation package, which might give some stimulus to the stock market.
"If it's well received, I think the stock market could have a boost, thus sustaining support for the rupiah," he said.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 on Friday.
